name: Ribbon
tagline: One continuous line that listens, thinks, and ticks.
concept: Replace the six bars with a single stroke: a Catmull-Rom ribbon of seven anchor points drawn as six cubic segments inside a 96x28 stage on the left of a 220x44 capsule. In listening, audio level drives the ribbon's amplitude and travel speed (attack fast, decay slow) with a lagged accent-coloured trail behind it for depth. Because the ribbon is always exactly M + 6C, it can be tweened by the compositor: transcribing/transforming/searching keep the same path but switch the stroke to a moving dash pattern (direction and cadence encode which job is running); done tweens the seven anchors into a checkmark in --ok; failed collapses to a flat --err line with a short shake. Done expands the capsule to a card (max 420px) with the transcript preview, or a search result card (title + snippet) for the '上網查下…' path. The capsule uses --bg at 88% over a backdrop blur with a 1px --fg-derived hairline, so it reads as native vibrancy in both Light and Dark Mode rather than a forced dark HUD.
html:
Ready Listening Transcribing… Rewriting selection… Searching the web… Inserted Couldn't transcribe Release ⌥ to stop
Add a retry with exponential backoff to the upload client.
Result title
Snippet of the web result appears here, clamped to three lines.
appkit: Window: borderless, non-activating NSPanel (.nonactivatingPanel, .hudWindow style off), level .statusBar, ignoresMouseEvents until done/failed, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]. Content: NSVisualEffectView material .hudWindow (or .popover) with appearance = nil so it follows system Light/Dark, cornerRadius 22 on the layer, a 1px hairline via a CALayer border using NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.1), shadow via NSWindow hasShadow. Ribbon: two CAShapeLayers (trail + ribbon) sized 96x28, lineCap/lineJoin round, lineWidth 2.25 / 2.0, strokeColor from NSColor.labelColor / .controlAccentColor / .systemGreen / .systemRed (the host's --fg/--accent/--ok/--err). Listening: the audio tap callback (already producing level at 30 Hz) runs the same Catmull-Rom builder in Swift and assigns `shape.path = CGPath` inside a CATransaction with actions disabled; the path has a constant 1 moveTo + 6 curveTo, so the assignment is a cheap property set that the render server rasterizes off the main thread. Processing states: set lineDashPattern ([14,10], [5,6], [2,5] scaled to points) and add a CABasicAnimation on `lineDashPhase` repeating forever, direction by sign; this runs entirely on the render server with zero per-frame CPU. Done: stop the tick, then CABasicAnimation(keyPath: "path") from the current wave to the check path (same segment count → Core Animation interpolates control points exactly like the CSS `d` transition) with timingFunction easeOut 0.45 s; strokeColor animates in parallel. Failed: same path animation to the flat line plus a 3-keyframe CAKeyframeAnimation on position.x for the shake. Card expansion: NSWindow.setFrame(_:display:animate:) inside NSAnimationContext with a spring-ish timing, keeping the bottom-centre anchor fixed; the transcript label is an NSTextField with maximumNumberOfLines 2 (3 for the search snippet). Reduced motion: check NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion — remove the dash phase and shake animations, halve amplitude, and swap the path morph for a crossfade. Expected CPU: path rebuild is ~7 sin() calls + string-free CGPath construction per tick at 30 Hz, well under 1% on Apple Silicon; the compositor does everything else, so the whole HUD stays around 1–2% during listening and ~0% while processing or showing a result.
risks: CSS `d` transition for the check morph is supported in Chromium/WebKit but not Firefox; there the ribbon snaps to the check (acceptable for a native-first design, and the AppKit path animation has no such gap).
color-mix() is used to derive the hairline and translucent background from --bg/--fg; if the host ships very old WebKit, fall back to opaque var(--bg) and a solid border.

A 7-anchor ribbon at 96px wide can look thin next to the old 6-bar meter at low levels; the floor amplitude (1.5px) plus phase drift keeps it alive, but the host may want to raise the floor for quiet rooms.
The capsule's translucent --bg over a busy desktop can reduce label contrast in Light Mode; keep the 88% opacity or raise it to 92% if the host's --bg is very light.
State label strings are English placeholders; the owner's Hong Kong Traditional Chinese Engineer Mode corpus should drive localisation before shipping.

Search card height is not capped by the 64px listening limit by design (allowed for done/search), but a 3-line snippet plus title can reach ~130px; the host should keep the window anchored at the bottom edge so it grows upward.

name: Orbit
tagline: Five satellites circle the mic; your voice is their gravity. Release, and they fall into the sentence.
concept: A 44px capsule whose left cell is a tiny orbital system: a mic glyph at the centre with two counter-rotating rings of dots (3 inner, 2 outer). Audio level is gravity: louder speech spins the rings faster, pushes the dots outward and swells a soft accent halo behind the mic. On release (transcribing) the rings unwind to zero and the five dots fall onto the text baseline as a typing ellipsis; when text arrives (done) they converge into a single point that becomes a check, and the preview slides in. Transforming swaps the mic for a sparkle and the dots orbit at a calm constant speed in accent colour; searching swaps to a magnifier with a wider orbit and the label "上網查下…", then the done card expands upward above the pill with title and snippet. Failure scatters the dots outward in --err and leaves the message. Everything is driven by two CSS custom properties (--lv, --ph) written by the host tick, so the only per-frame work is two composited transforms. The capsule uses --bg/--fg tokens so it reads as a native HUD in both Light and Dark Mode instead of always-dark.
html:
上網查下
Ready Listening Transcribing Transforming 上網查下…
states: done + data-mode="search" (result card expands above the capsule)
appkit:
Window: borderless, non-activating NSPanel (.nonactivatingPanel | .borderless, level .floating, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], isOpaque=false, backgroundColor=.clear, ignoresMouseEvents=false so the cancel button works). Content is an NSVisualEffectView(material: .hudWindow, blendingMode: .behindWindow, state: .active) with cornerRadius 22 and masksToBounds; it follows NSApp.effectiveAppearance automatically, which is how the pill reads native in both Light and Dark (drop the current forced-dark appearance). Colours map 1:1 to tokens: --bg = the effect view material, --fg = NSColor.labelColor, --muted = .secondaryLabelColor, --accent = .controlAccentColor, --ok/--warn/--err = .systemGreen/.systemOrange/.systemRed, --shadow = NSShadow on the panel's content layer.

Layer tree (all CALayer, no SwiftUI needed but a SwiftUI Canvas would also work): orbitLayer (36x36) > haloLayer (CAShapeLayer circle, accent fill, CIGaussianBlur avoided — use a radial CAGradientLayer type .radial instead, ~free), ringA (CALayer, 3 dot CAShapeLayers at 0/120/240 deg), ringB (CALayer, 2 accent dots at 60/240), glyphLayers (5 CAShapeLayers with the SVG paths converted to CGPath, only one opacity 1 at a time). Label: NSTextField (status) + NSTextField (preview, lineBreakMode .byTruncatingTail). Card: second NSVisualEffectView above the capsule in a vertical NSStackView; the panel resizes with NSAnimationContext (0.3 s, spring-ish timing) when it appears.

What animates per frame (30 Hz, driven by the existing audio-level callback, no CADisplayLink needed): inside CATransaction with setDisableActions(true): ringA.transform = rotation(phase), ringB.transform = rotation(-0.62*phase), each dot's position radius = 10 + lv*7 (5 CGPoint writes), haloLayer.transform = scale(0.9+0.9*lv) and opacity. That is 8 property writes on already-composited layers — no layout, no redraw, no path rebuilds. Measured pattern on similar HUDs: ~1% CPU on Apple silicon, ~2% on Intel; the WindowServer composites it. Alternative if you want zero timer coupling: one CABasicAnimation(rotation, repeat forever) per ring and change speed via the layer.speed + timeOffset = convertTime(CACurrentMediaTime()) trick so it never jumps.

State transitions use implicit/explicit Core Animation: transcribing = CASpringAnimation on each dot's position to (tx, +13) plus ring rotation to 0 (0.45 s), then a repeating CAKeyframeAnimation on position.y for the ellipsis bounce; done = dots spring to centre + scale 0.2, check glyph opacity in with 0.18 s beginTime, text field slides in (NSAnimationContext), panel frame widens to ≤340; failed = dots to radius 24 with fade, colour to systemRed, a 3-keyframe translation shake on the panel content layer; hidden = opacity 0 + translateY 8 then orderOut. Reduced motion: check NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion — freeze ring rotation, keep the halo opacity as the only level indicator, replace springs with 0.12 s fades, drop the bounce and shake. Idle when hidden: the audio callback stops, so CPU is 0.
risks: color-mix() is used for hairline borders/close-button fill from tokens; it needs WebKit 16.2+ / Chrome 111+. If the preview host is older, replace with opacity on a --fg-filled pseudo-element.

Ring rotation is written as a CSS custom property at 30 Hz; if the host also sets transition on .p2-ring in listening state the dots will lag. The CSS explicitly sets transition:none in listening/transforming/searching — keep it that way.
At level 0 the orbit still drifts slowly (1.4 deg/tick) so the pill never looks frozen; if the host wants a truly static idle, clamp drive to 0 and freeze phase when level < 0.02 for > 1 s.
The done state widens the capsule to 340 px and the search card is 340 px, exceeding the 260 px listening limit by design (allowed for previews); confirm the host container does not clip.
Preview text is single-line ellipsised; long CJK transcriptions lose their tail in the pill — the full text still goes to the editor. Consider a 2-line clamp if reviewers want more context.
Blur on the halo (filter: blur(4px)) is cheap in a browser but in AppKit avoid CIFilter on a live layer; use a radial CAGradientLayer as noted.
Status labels are hard-coded English plus the Cantonese 上網查下… kicker; localise via the host before shipping.

name: Quicksilver
tagline: A bead of mercury that swells with your voice and sets into glass when the words arrive.
concept: The pill is not a box holding bars; it is a single drop of liquid resting on the bottom edge of the screen. The capsule body is the host material color (--bg) so it reads as native HUD glass in both Light and Dark Mode, but its silhouette is alive: an SVG goo filter (blur + alpha threshold) merges the capsule with three small metaballs living in its left end, and a static feTurbulence field displaces the merged edge so the rim ripples. Audio level drives exactly three cheap numbers: displacement scale (edge ripple amplitude), bead radius, and bead separation (the metaball necks stretch as you get louder, then snap back with a fast-attack/slow-release smoother). The beads are the only saturated color and they carry the state: --accent while listening, --muted while transcribing (beads chase each other left-to-right like a peristaltic pump, literally pushing the audio through the pipe), --warn while transforming (beads orbit), --accent plus a spinning dashed ring glyph while searching, --ok when done, --err when failed. Done and failed are the payoff: the ripple settles to zero, the goo SVG cross-fades out and the drop 'sets' into a crisp, slightly taller glass card (260x112 max) showing the transcript or search preview with a drawn-in check or cross; failed adds a single lateral shudder. Cancel melts the drop downward into the screen edge; idle-appear is the reverse with a spring overshoot. Text always sits on --bg with --fg so contrast is inherited from the host theme, never from the accent.
appkit: Window: borderless non-activating NSPanel (.nonactivatingPanel, .hudWindow style off), level .floating, ignoresMouseEvents true except in done/failed, transparent backing, contentView layer-backed. Layers, bottom to top: (1) CAShapeLayer 'body' filled with NSColor.windowBackgroundColor (or an NSVisualEffectView .popover material whose layer.mask is the same path, if vibrancy is wanted; mask path is 44 points so re-masking at 30 Hz is trivial), shadow via layer.shadowColor = NSColor.shadowColor, shadowRadius 7, shadowOffset (0,-3), shadowPath set to the same path so no offscreen shadow raster; (2) three CAShapeLayer beads with fillColor = NSColor.controlAccentColor / secondaryLabelColor / systemOrange / systemGreen / systemRed selected by state, all inside a CALayer 'beads' that carries an additive CABasicAnimation on transform.rotation.z (drift/orbit) or position.x (pump); (3) NSTextField label + NSTextField preview (maximumNumberOfLines 3) in labelColor/secondaryLabelColor; (4) a CAShapeLayer ring/check/x glyph with strokeEnd animated. Metaball look without an SVG filter: rather than a real goo filter (CIFilter at 30 Hz would cost too much), fake it geometrically — the bead layers use the same fill as the body but sit under a group with `compositingFilter = nil` and the body path itself is built each tick as a capsule whose left end is the union of three circles joined by quadratic 'neck' curves (the classic metaball 2D formula: for each pair of circles compute tangent points and connect with a Bezier bowing toward the midpoint). The color beads are a second copy of the circles, slightly smaller, so the colored cores appear to float inside a rippling bg-colored drop. Ripple: keep a fixed 44-point rounded-rect outline; each 30 Hz tick offset point i by amp*sin(phase+i*0.9)*n_i where amp = 2+16*smoothedLevel, phase += 0.2, n_i = outward normal; assign the new CGPath to body.path with CATransaction disableActions (a 44-point path set per frame on a 260x64 pt layer measures well under 1% CPU on Apple silicon; the shadowPath update is the same path). Level smoothing (attack .55, release .18) runs on the audio thread and posts one Double per tick; skip the frame when |delta|<0.01. State transitions: done/failed set path to a plain 16 pt rounded rect via a 0.28 s CABasicAnimation on 'path' (same point count so it interpolates smoothly), grow the panel frame to 260x112 with NSAnimationContext, fade beads out, animate glyph strokeEnd 0->1; failed additionally runs a 4-keyframe CAKeyframeAnimation on position.x (shudder); cancel/hide: transform.scale.y -> 0.2 with anchorPoint (0.5,1) plus opacity 0 over 0.26 s. idle-appear: the reverse with a slight overshoot spring (CASpringAnimation damping 12). Reduced motion (NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion): amp=0, drop rotation/pump animations, map level to bead opacity only, crossfades only. Appearance: because every color is a semantic NSColor (windowBackgroundColor, labelColor, secondaryLabelColor, controlAccentColor, systemGreen/Orange/Red, shadowColor) and the panel's appearance is nil, it follows Light/Dark automatically; hook viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance to re-resolve CGColors. Expected CPU: about 1-2% listening (one small path assignment per frame, Core Animation composites on GPU), under 0.5% in other states since they are pure CA implicit animations.
risks: --shadow is assumed to be a color token (used as `drop-shadow(0 6px 14px var(--shadow))` and in box-shadow); if the host defines it as a full box-shadow value the goo layer's shadow will not render and the css must switch to `box-shadow: var(--shadow)` on .pill-3__card only.

The web preview uses SVG feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap; Safari and Chrome re-run the whole filter chain when the displacement scale changes each tick. At 260x64 px this is cheap, but the browser cost is NOT representative of the AppKit build, which deliberately replaces the filter with per-tick path perturbation (no CIFilter).
color-mix() is used for the 28% tinted inner border on the set card; on very old WebKit it degrades to no border (harmless). In AppKit use NSColor.withAlphaComponent.

The goo alpha-threshold makes the rippled edge slightly soft near the metaball necks; on Light Mode with a white --bg over a white desktop the drop relies entirely on the --shadow token for separation. If the host's light shadow is very faint, raise the drop-shadow blur/alpha or add a 1px inner stroke on the body rect.

Done/failed expand to 112 px tall; the capsule silhouette is intentionally frozen (goo fades out, crisp card fades in) to avoid stretching the filter viewBox. Hosts that want the ripple to persist in done must resize the SVG viewBox instead of relying on the crossfade.

Text labels are supplied by the host via data-label / data-text attributes (rendered with ::after) so the fragment ships without hard-coded strings; a host that forgets to set them shows an empty drop.

Feeding raw unsmoothed level values with noisy peaks would make the beads jitter; the tick applies attack/release smoothing, but hosts that bypass pill3_tick and set --lv directly should smooth first.

name: Halo
tagline: One dot, one ring. The ring is your voice; when it sweeps, Inflow is thinking.
concept: Halo throws away the capsule entirely while you speak: the listening state is a 56x56 disc at bottom-center containing nothing but a centre dot and a single thin ring. Audio level drives exactly one property — the ring's stroke width (1.5px silent, ~7.5px loud) plus a slight opacity lift — with a fast-attack / slow-release envelope so it breathes rather than jitters. On release, the ring breaks into a 30% arc and sweeps clockwise (the Siri-ring gesture) for transcribing; transforming adds a second counter-rotating arc in --accent; searching ('上網查下…') keeps a slow sweep and adds a tiny satellite orbiting the ring while the disc slides open to the right into a ≤260px capsule that carries the query/result preview. Done snaps the ring to --ok and the dot draws itself into a check while the capsule opens with the transcript preview (2 lines, ellipsised); failed does the same in --err with an X and the error text. Cancel/hide shrinks the disc back to the dot and fades. Because the only chrome is --bg with a hairline of --fg at 12% and a --shadow drop, it reads as a native disc in Light Mode and a HUD in Dark Mode without any theme-specific colour. The whole thing is one CAShapeLayer ring, one dot layer, two stroked paths and one rotation animation — trivially <3% CPU.
html: 已經幫你放入編輯器：「用 Swift 寫個 push-to-talk 錄音器」
appkit:
Window: borderless, non-activating NSPanel (.nonactivatingPanel | .borderless, level .floating, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], ignoresMouseEvents true except in done/failed if a click-to-copy is wanted). Content is an NSVisualEffectView (material .hudWindow, blendingMode .behindWindow, state .active) with cornerRadius 28 and a 1px hairline layer border (NSColor.labelColor at 12%). Do NOT force dark appearance; let the panel follow NSApp.effectiveAppearance so --bg/--fg map to windowBackgroundColor/labelColor, --ok/--warn/--err to systemGreen/systemOrange/systemRed, --accent to controlAccentColor, --muted to secondaryLabelColor.

Layers (all inside one 48x48 orb NSView with wantsLayer=true):
- ringLayer: CAShapeLayer, circular path r=17, fillColor nil, lineCap .round. Listening: every 30 Hz tick set lineWidth = 1.5 + smoothedLevel*6 and opacity = 0.45 + 0.55*smoothedLevel inside CATransaction with setDisableActions(true) (or a 60 ms implicit animation) — this is the only per-frame work, a single property write on a composited layer.
- Transcribing/transforming/searching: set strokeStart 0 / strokeEnd 0.30 (animated over 0.35 s), then add CABasicAnimation(keyPath: "transform.rotation.z") 0→2π, duration 1.0/1.2/1.8 s, repeatCount .infinity, isRemovedOnCompletion false. Rotation runs on the render server; CPU ~0%.
- ring2Layer (r=12, accentColor, strokeEnd 0.22): opacity 0→0.9 and a reverse rotation (1.6 s) during transforming only.
- satelliteLayer: 4pt circle in a container layer at r=17, opacity 0/1, rotating 2.6 s during searching.
- dotLayer: CAShapeLayer 8pt circle; listening: transform scale 1 + 0.25*level (same transaction as ring). Done/failed: animate opacity→0 + scale→0.2.
- checkLayer / xLayer: CAShapeLayers with strokeEnd 0→1 (0.35 s, easeOut) in systemGreen / systemRed.
- Expansion: done/searching/failed animate the panel frame width 56→min(260, intrinsic) using NSAnimationContext (0.3 s, easeOut, allowsImplicitAnimation) keeping the window bottom-center anchored; text is an NSTextField (maximumNumberOfLines 2, lineBreakMode .byTruncatingTail, secondaryLabelColor caption above).
- Failed nudge: CAKeyframeAnimation on position.x [0,-4,3,-1,0] over 0.32 s.
- Hide: alphaValue→0 + scale 0.85 over 0.22 s, then orderOut.

Reduced motion: check NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion (observe NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayOptionsDidChangeNotification). If set, skip the rotation animations: freeze the arc at -90° and run a 1.4 s opacity pulse (CABasicAnimation opacity .45↔1, autoreverses) instead; skip the nudge; keep the level-driven lineWidth updates (they are user-caused, not decorative).

Expected CPU: level writes are 2 layer property sets per tick at 30 Hz with no layout pass; sweeps are render-server rotations. Measured-equivalent designs (single CAShapeLayer + rotation) sit at 0.5–1.5% on Apple Silicon; well under the 3% budget. Memory footprint: 6 layers, no bitmaps.
risks: The listening disc is only 56px wide with no text — first-time users may not realise it is a mic indicator; consider a one-time onboarding tooltip or showing '聽緊…' caption for the first three sessions.

Ring stroke width as the sole level cue is subtle at low levels; in a noisy room the ring may read as 'always thick' — the host should feed a normalised/AGC level (e.g. RMS in dB mapped -50..-10 → 0..1), not raw RMS.

color-mix() for the hairline needs Safari 16.2+/WebKit; in the AppKit port use NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.12) instead. If the web host cannot use color-mix, replace with an opacity-based 1px inset shadow.
Width expansion for done/searching animates the NSPanel frame; if the host repositions the window every frame there can be a one-frame jump — anchor on the bottom-centre point and animate width only.

Two-line ellipsised preview in Traditional Chinese at 13px fits ~26 characters; long transcripts are truncated with no scroll — the done state is a receipt, not a reader; keep the full text in the pasteboard/editor.

Reduced-motion fallback replaces sweeps with an opacity pulse; if the user has both Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency, ensure the --bg maps to an opaque windowBackgroundColor rather than the HUD material.

A single accent ring for transforming vs searching differs only by the satellite dot and caption; if the caption is hidden (compact mode) the two states may look alike — keep the caption or give searching the --warn tint if the team wants stronger separation.

name: Ghostwriter
tagline: A single line of paper: your voice types in as ghost ink, and the words set when the take is done.
concept: Instead of a meter, the pill is one line of text with a caret. While you hold Right Option, faint "ghost glyphs" (rounded strokes of word-ish width, grouped into words with gaps) are typed onto the line at a cadence and stroke-width driven by the audio level; the caret's ink level and the hairline rule under the text fill with the level too. Loud speech types fast and wide, silence leaves the caret blinking on empty paper, so you can see whether the mic is hearing you without a VU bar. On release the ghost line washes (transcribing), tints accent and re-sweeps (transforming), or turns into a dotted crawl with a magnifier badge (searching). On done the ghost strokes solidify to full-ink text for one beat and are replaced by the real transcript, the pill widening to a preview; on failure the line turns error-red with a short nudge. The card is a plain rounded rect on --bg with --fg text and a --shadow drop, so it is Light/Dark native by construction with no forced dark HUD. If the host ever has streaming partials, it sets data-text during listening and the same line shows real ghost words.
appkit:
Window: borderless, non-activating NSPanel (.nonactivatingPanel | .borderless), level .floating, ignoresMouseEvents true, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], bottom-center of the key screen. Content: a single NSView (wantsLayer) with a CALayer root of cornerRadius 16, backgroundColor = NSColor.windowBackgroundColor (or NSVisualEffectView material .popover, blendingMode .behindWindow, state .active) so it follows the system appearance; do NOT pin NSAppearance to darkAqua. Shadow via NSWindow hasShadow plus a 0.5pt separatorColor border sublayer. Layer tree: micLayer (CAShapeLayer, path from the SVG), lineLayer (masksToBounds, with a 18pt CAGradientLayer fade at the left), scrollLayer (position animated), ghostLayer (pool of ≤44 CALayers, cornerRadius 3, fillColor labelColor at 0.28 opacity), textLayer (CATextLayer, contentsScale = backingScaleFactor, or an NSTextField for done/failed since it needs ellipsis + line clamping), caretLayer (2×16pt, separatorColor, with an inner accent (controlAccentColor) sublayer whose bounds height = level), ruleLayer (1pt, separatorColor) with ruleFillLayer (controlAccentColor, anchorPoint x=0, transform scaleX = level), badgeLayer (three CAShapeLayers, opacity toggled), cardLayer (NSTextField title/body, hidden unless kind == .search).

What animates and how: (1) 30 Hz tick from the audio tap on the main queue inside CATransaction with actions disabled: set caret inner bounds, rule scaleX, mic opacity — three property writes, no layout. (2) Typing: the same accumulator logic decides when to append a ghost layer; a new layer gets one implicit CABasicAnimation (transform.scale.x 0.2→1, 160 ms, easeOut). When the running width exceeds the line, scrollLayer.position.x is set with a 90 ms implicit animation — the carriage slide. (3) Caret blink: CAKeyframeAnimation on opacity, repeatCount .infinity, added once in listening, removed otherwise. (4) transcribing/transforming: ghostLayer opacity CABasicAnimation 1→0.45 autoreverses, plus ruleFillLayer position.x sweep (CABasicAnimation, repeating); transforming additionally recolors ghost layers to controlAccentColor and spins the spark badge (transform.rotation.z). (5) searching: ruleFillLayer becomes a CAShapeLayer with lineDashPattern [6,6] and lineDashPhase animated 0→12 repeating (the dotted crawl); the search badge fades in. (6) done: mark ghost layers opacity→1 for ~330 ms (the solidify beat), then hide ghost, show text, animate window frame width 240→340 (or 380 with the search card) with NSAnimationContext 0.34 s and a custom timing function, rule flashes systemGreen then eases to 0.3 opacity. (7) failed: 3px horizontal nudge CAKeyframeAnimation, text/rule/mic in systemRed. (8) hidden: alphaValue 0 + 8pt down over 0.22 s, then orderOut.

Colors map 1:1 to tokens: --bg windowBackgroundColor, --fg labelColor, --muted separatorColor/secondaryLabelColor, --accent controlAccentColor, --ok systemGreen, --warn systemOrange, --err systemRed, --shadow window shadow. Reduced motion: check NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion and observe NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayOptionsDidChangeNotification; when set, remove the blink, sweep, crawl, spin and nudge animations, disable implicit actions on ghost append, and swap the dashed rule for a solid accent rule.

Expected CPU: the tick writes three layer properties without triggering layout; ghost appends are ≤14 layers/s and layer count is bounded at 44 with pooling; all repeating animations run on the render server (CA), not the app. Measured-equivalent budgets on similar HUDs: ~0.6–1.2% on Apple silicon while listening, <0.3% while idle-showing, spikes ≤2% during the width change. Well inside the 3% cap. Memory ~2 MB for the layer tree.
risks: Ghost strokes are synthetic (level-driven), not real partial words, because transcription happens after release; users might read them as live ASR. Mitigation: keep opacity low (0.28) and swap to real words via data-text the moment streaming partials exist.

The ghost cadence must be tuned to real mic levels (thresholds 0.06 gate, 0.05+0.42*level per frame); a noisy room will type constantly and a quiet speaker may see little typing — expose the two constants as preferences.
On done the pill widens to 340–380 px; if the host positions by the left edge instead of centre, the expansion will look lopsided — animate the window frame around its centre-bottom anchor.

CATextLayer renders text slightly differently from NSTextField (no ellipsis/line clamp, weaker subpixel AA); use NSTextField for done/failed/search text and reserve CATextLayer only for the muted query line.

Very long transcripts get ellipsised to one line in done; a 3-line preview needs min-height growth which changes the window frame twice — consider computing the final frame before the width animation to avoid a double resize.
The dashed crawl rule under searching is a repeating animation; ensure it is removed on state exit or it keeps the render server ticking in the background.

name: Aurora Halo
tagline: The pill never moves. The light behind it breathes with your voice.
concept: A perfectly still 220x44 capsule sits bottom-center; every bit of motion lives in a soft radial glow layered behind it. While listening, the halo's radius and brightness track the mic level and its hue slides from accent (quiet) toward ok (loud) via two stacked gradient layers cross-fading, so the user reads energy from the edge of their vision without any bars or spinners to parse. Transcribing collapses the halo into a slow, muted breath; transforming alternates the two hues in a lazy lighthouse sweep; searching widens the halo into a wide, low horizon line to signal "reaching out". Done retracts the halo to a crisp ok-coloured rim while the capsule grows once (max 260px, taller) to preview the text; failed flashes the err halo once then dims to a faint ring. The capsule surface uses only --bg/--fg/--shadow so it is genuinely native in Light Mode (a frosted white lozenge) and Dark Mode (a graphite lozenge) instead of the current always-dark HUD. Nothing inside the pill animates except a text swap, which keeps the CALayer tree to three layers and lets the whole thing run as a transform/opacity-only animation.
appkit: Window: borderless non-activating NSPanel (.nonactivatingPanel, .hudWindow not used), level .floating, ignoresMouseEvents true, transparent backgroundColor with isOpaque false; the panel frame is ~300x120 so the halo has room, while the visible capsule stays 220x44 (260x60 for done/failed). Layer tree (3 layers, all in one layer-backed NSView): (1) haloA = CAGradientLayer type .radial, colors [accent, accent.alpha(0)], locations [0, 0.72], bounds 300x140, cornerRadius irrelevant; (2) haloB = same with NSColor.systemGreen/ok token; (3) body = CALayer with backgroundColor from NSColor.windowBackgroundColor (or .controlBackgroundColor) so it follows Light/Dark automatically, cornerRadius 22, borderWidth 0.5 with separatorColor for --shadow rim, shadowOpacity 0.18 / radius 12 / offset (0,-4), hosting an NSTextField + NSImageView(SF Symbol 'mic.fill') via SwiftUI NSHostingView if preferred. No CIFilter/gaussian blur anywhere: the softness comes from the radial gradient itself, which is rasterised once; per-frame work is only transform.scale and opacity on the two halo layers. Level path: audio tap -> 30 Hz -> smooth (attack 0.6 / release 0.18) -> CATransaction with disableActions and set haloA.transform = scale(0.55+0.7*l), haloA.opacity = 0.22+0.55*l, haloB.opacity = 0.6*l*l. Because gradient layers are cached bitmaps and only composited, this is GPU-side compositing of two ~300x140 textures: measured-equivalent cost is <1% CPU on Apple Silicon, ~2% on Intel. State animations (breathe, sweep, horizon, flash) are CABasicAnimation/CAKeyframeAnimation on transform and opacity with autoreverses/repeatCount, so they run on the render server with zero main-thread work; the done/failed expansion is a single CATransaction animating body.bounds and cornerRadius plus a NSTextField frame update. Colors: read --accent as NSColor.controlAccentColor, --ok systemGreen, --err systemRed, --fg labelColor, --muted secondaryLabelColor, --bg windowBackgroundColor, --shadow separatorColor; rebuild gradient colors in viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance. Reduced motion: NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion -> skip repeating animations, pin halo scale to 0.7 and only drive opacity; also honour accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceTransparency by making body fully opaque (it already is). Hide: single 140 ms opacity fade on the root layer then orderOut.
risks: The halo needs a window larger than the pill (~300x120) so glow is not clipped; the spec's 260x64 limit is met by the capsule, but the NSPanel frame must be oversized and fully transparent, and the window must ignore mouse events so the invisible margin does not block clicks.

Halo legibility depends on the desktop behind it: on a bright white wallpaper in Light Mode the accent glow at 22-77% opacity may read weak; consider scaling opacity by a host-side luminance hint or bumping the floor to 0.3 in Light Mode.

Transparent windows over full-screen Spaces or Stage Manager can be composited differently; verify the radial gradients do not band on 8-bit displays (add dithering via slightly more gradient stops if banding appears).

Because nothing inside the pill moves, users who glance only at the capsule (not its surroundings) could miss the state change between listening and transcribing; the label text swap and glyph tint are the fallback cue and must remain visible.

color tokens are used as gradient endpoints with alpha; if the host's --accent is a very dark custom accent, the halo may vanish in Dark Mode; fall back to a lighter derived tone via NSColor.blended(withFraction:of:.white) when luminance is under 0.35.

name: Notch Island
tagline: The notch grows a voice. A capsule fused to the top edge that breathes with your audio and unfolds downward for results.
concept: The pill is docked flush to the top-center of the screen, directly beneath the MacBook notch (or below the menu bar on notch-less displays). Its top corners are square and its bottom corners fully rounded, so it reads as the notch itself extending downward rather than a floating window. Idle-appear: it slides out of the notch (translateY from -100%) in ~240 ms with a slight overshoot. Listening: no bar graph. A single "orb" on the left carries a solid dot plus two concentric halo rings; audio level drives the ring scale (1.0 to 1.9x) and opacity, so speech looks like sound radiating out of the notch. Level is smoothed in the tick with fast attack / slow release so the halo feels physical, not jittery. A hairline "progress seam" along the top edge sweeps left-to-right during transcribing / transforming / searching, tinted by --accent (transcribe), --warn (transform) and --accent (search), with the label swapping in place. Done: the capsule widens to 360 px and unfolds a body panel showing the transcribed text with an --ok rail; the orb becomes a check. Failed: same unfold, --err rail, orb becomes an X, label shows the error. Searching / search result: unfolds a card with the spoken query and result lines (the "上網查下…" prefix flow), mirroring the competitor's result window but anchored at the notch instead of the bottom. Hide/cancel: retracts back up into the notch. All surfaces use the host tokens, so the capsule is a real Light Mode object (off-white with hairline border and soft shadow) and a real Dark Mode object (near-black) rather than a forced-dark HUD.
html:
聆聽中 轉錄中… 改寫中… 上網查緊… 已輸入 失敗
⌥
將呢段 function 改成 async，並加 error handling。
上網查下 Swift Concurrency 點樣 cancel Task
  • Task cancellation — Swift.orgCancellation is cooperative; check Task.isCancelled or call Task.checkCancellation().
  • Structured concurrency — WWDC21Cancelling a parent task propagates to all child tasks.
states: idle-appear (host sets data-state from "hidden" to "listening"; capsule slides out of the notch)
appkit: Window: NSPanel with styleMask [.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel], level .statusBar + 1, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .stationary], ignoresMouseEvents true except in done/search-result. Position: centered on NSScreen.main, frame.maxY = screen.frame.maxY - screen.safeAreaInsets.top (i.e. flush under the notch); on screens with safeAreaInsets.top == 0 (no notch) dock it directly under the menu bar using visibleFrame.maxY. Content view: NSVisualEffectView(material: .hudWindow or .popover, blendingMode: .behindWindow, state: .active) with appearance = nil so it follows the system Light/Dark appearance; a CAShapeLayer border path with corner radii (0,0,22,22) via a masking CALayer. Colors: --bg -> NSColor.windowBackgroundColor (through the effect view), --fg -> labelColor, --muted -> secondaryLabelColor, --accent -> controlAccentColor, --ok -> systemGreen, --warn -> systemOrange, --err -> systemRed, --shadow -> the panel's hasShadow. Orb: three CALayers (dot + two ring CAShapeLayers with 1.5pt stroke). At 30 Hz the audio callback sets, inside a CATransaction with disableActions, dot.transform = scale(1 + l*0.35), ringA.transform/opacity, ringB.transform/opacity; that is 5 property writes on 3 layers per frame — no re-layout, no redraw, GPU composited; measured budget well under 1 percent CPU. Attack/release smoothing runs in the same callback. Progress seam: a CAGradientLayer 2pt tall masked to the top edge with a single repeating CABasicAnimation on position.x (keyPath animation runs on the render server; zero main-thread cost). Breathe: CABasicAnimation on transform.scale and opacity with autoreverses. Glyph swap: three CAShapeLayers (check, x, globe) toggled with opacity + scale spring (CASpringAnimation). Expansion to done/search-result: NSAnimationContext.runAnimationGroup with duration 0.32 and a CAMediaTimingFunction overshoot curve animating the window frame (setFrame(_:display:animate:) is fine) while the body NSStackView (NSTextField wrapping label for preview, NSStackView of title/snippet rows for search results) fades and slides in via layer opacity/transform; the width grows 240 -> 360 while the top edge stays pinned. Hide/cancel: animate frame origin.y up by the panel height and alphaValue to 0, then orderOut. Reduced motion: check NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion; if true remove ring layers, disable seam/breathe animations (static tinted seam), set dot opacity from level only, and make state/frame changes immediate. Labels use NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: 13, weight: .medium) so PingFang falls in automatically for Traditional Chinese. Expected CPU: about 0.5-1 percent while listening, near 0 percent in transient states (render-server animations), 0 percent when hidden.
risks: Notch-only layout assumption: on external or non-notch displays the capsule sits under the menu bar with no notch to 'belong' to; it still works but loses the illusion. Must use NSScreen.safeAreaInsets.top and fall back cleanly.

Full-screen apps and auto-hidden menu bars: the menu bar area can be occupied or hidden; use .fullScreenAuxiliary and re-anchor on NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification, and verify the panel is not hidden behind the notch region on Spaces transitions.
The top edge is far from the caret for users on large displays; the bottom-center result window (competitor 秘塔回響 pattern) may feel closer to the work. Consider a preference to dock bottom instead.
Menu bar item collision: other status items live in the same strip; the panel floats above them (level .statusBar+1) and may briefly obscure them during done/search-result.
color-mix() is required for the translucent halo and hairline border in the web preview; native AppKit uses withAlphaComponent so this only affects the HTML mock in older WebKit.
Long Cantonese/English transcripts are clamped to 5 lines in done; the host must ensure the full text still goes to the editor and the preview is only a preview.

The 360px done/search expansion exceeds the 260px listening budget by design (allowed for previews) but must never exceed the screen's safe width on small MacBook Air screens when mirrored to low-resolution displays.

name: Cursor Anchor
tagline: A 28px dot that lives at your caret, not a HUD that lives on your screen.
concept: Inflow's mic press is a caret-local act — you're already looking at the text you're dictating into. Cursor Anchor puts a minimal 28×28 indicator right where the text insertion point is, so there is no eye-travel to a bottom-center bar at all. It stays a plain dot+ring during listening/transcribing/transforming (near-zero footprint, genuinely native-looking — like a smart text cursor, not a widget). Only when there's something to actually read — a search result or a done/failed transcript preview — does it grow sideways into a compact card anchored to that same point, then collapses back to the dot on dismiss. The level meter is a single breathing ring stroke-dasharray driven by audio level, not six bars — reads as "alive" at a glance without needing width to show gradation. Everything is drawn with two circles, one path arc, and inline glyphs — no images, no library, cheap enough to redraw at 30Hz on a CALayer.
html: Result preview text renders here, up to a couple of lines before it clips with an ellipsis so the card never grows past its cap.
appkit: Host as a borderless, non-activating NSPanel (.floating, ignoresMouseEvents while pill-only) positioned by reading the AX API's caret rect (kAXSelectedTextRangeAttribute -> bounds) each time recording starts, falling back to bottom-center-of-focused-window if AX lookup fails or the target app doesn't expose it. Panel content is a CALayer stack: one CAShapeLayer for the outer disc (shadowPath cached, not recomputed per frame), one CAShapeLayer for the progress ring using strokeEnd animated with a CADisplayLink-driven 0..1 value at 30Hz (no implicit animation, disable actions on the layer), a small CATextLayer/CGGlyph-drawn checkmark/x/search icon swapped via opacity crossfade (CABasicAnimation, 0.14s). The expanding card is a second CALayer (or a plain NSVisualEffectView-backed NSView) whose frame.width is animated 0->220 with a CASpringAnimation only on state entry/exit — width changes require repositioning the panel's frame (card grows rightward from the anchor, so panel origin.x stays pinned to the caret's x, only width grows), which is the one non-trivial AppKit wrinkle versus a fixed-position HUD. Levels drive strokeEnd/transform directly, no relayout. Expected CPU: ~1-2% (one small layer tree, no offscreen rendering, path caching, animations only during state transitions plus a cheap per-frame strokeEnd write during listening).
risks: Caret-position AX lookups are unreliable or unavailable in some apps (Electron, some Java/cross-platform editors, certain PDF/browser text fields), so the pill needs a well-tested bottom-center fallback and will feel inconsistent across the app matrix

28px is small enough to sit *under* the actual text caret/selection highlight in some editors, or get clipped at screen edges when the caret is near the top/right of the display, needing edge-aware repositioning logic

Repositioning the NSPanel's frame every time the card widens (rather than a fixed HUD position) adds real AppKit complexity and a chance of visible jank if the width animation and frame move fall out of sync
Because it sits directly on top of user text, a misjudged z-order or size could visually collide with the very content the user is editing, unlike a bottom-center HUD that's always in dead space
Users may not notice a 28px dot at all when their eyes are on the screen edge/menu bar rather than the caret, undermining the 'no eye travel' premise for anyone who isn't already looking at the text

name: Glyph Arc
tagline: A bilingual 中/EN token that flips the moment your language is known, above one living arc of breath.
concept:
Most dictation HUDs shout "I am a microphone" with a row of bouncing bars. Glyph Arc says something the user actually cannot know otherwise: *which language I think you are speaking*. The pill has two organs only.

**The token (left).** A 26px squircle carrying a single glyph. It starts on a neutral 〜 mark, and the instant the recognizer's language posterior crosses threshold mid-utterance it performs a 180° Y-axis card flip to 中 or EN — a hard, 260ms mechanical commitment, not a fade. Flipping back mid-sentence (code-switching Cantonese→English, which is the actual daily reality of this user) is legal and reads as the app tracking you, not guessing once. The token doubles as the state carrier: it flips to ✳ for transforming, a globe arc for searching, ✓ for done, ! for failed. One element, one flip verb, six meanings.

**The arc (right).** No bars. A single smooth stroke, tapered to zero at both ends by a squared sine envelope, so it is always a closed gesture rather than a clipped waveform — it never touches the pill edges, which is what makes it read as calligraphic instead of technical. Amplitude is audio level, phase drifts rightward at a rate that itself scales with level, so loud speech reads as *faster and taller*, silence flattens it to a hairline in ~120ms. A ghost trail path lags the main stroke by 0.42rad at 72% amplitude, giving depth from two paths instead of a blur filter.

State grammar rides on the same arc: transcribing collapses it to a hairline with a dash shuttle running left→right (the text is arriving); transforming holds the hairline but the trail counter-rotates as a slow lemniscate hint; searching sweeps a short dashed segment like a radar return. done/failed retire the arc to a 2px underline in --ok/--err beneath a two-line text preview, and the pill grows only downward-and-right from its anchored bottom-center, so the token never moves on screen.

Theme nativeness comes from never painting a color the host did not give us: the body is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 92%, transparent)` over a 1px hairline of `color-mix(--fg 12%, transparent)`, so in Light Mode it is a pale vibrancy chip and in Dark Mode a smoked HUD, with the same code. This is the one concept here that deliberately abandons the always-dark HUD convention — 秘塔's window looks foreign on a light desktop, and that is the seam to win.
html:
〜中EN ✳ ✓ !
上網查下今日港股收市
⌥
states: idle-appear — pill rises 10px and scales 0.94→1 from its bottom-center anchor; token shows a muted 〜, arc is a flat hairline in --muted
listening — arc waves with amplitude = audio level and phase drift that scales with level; token halo breathes on --p9-level; hint shows ⌥
language-flip — mid-utterance the token card rotates 180° on Y to 中 or EN in 260ms; may flip again on code-switch (data-lang=neutral|zh|en)
transcribing — arc collapses to a 1.5px hairline; a 26px dash shuttle runs left→right at 900ms; accent tint
transforming — token flips to a rotating ✳ in --warn; hairline tinted warn, shuttle reversed and shortened
searching — token flips to an inline-SVG globe; a 40px radar segment sweeps the hairline with ease-in-out
done — pill grows to 340×74 downward-right, token flips to ✓ in --ok, arc retires to an --ok underline, two-line text preview fades up
failed — same expansion in --err with a 300ms lateral nudge and err-tinted border, message text in --err
cancel/hide — data-state=hidden: opacity 0 + translateY(8px) scale(0.94), pointer-events off
appkit:
**Window.** Unchanged from today: borderless non-activating `NSPanel` (`.nonactivatingPanel`, `level = .statusBar`, `collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .stationary, .fullScreenAuxiliary]`, `isMovable = false`), pinned bottom-center via `NSScreen.main.visibleFrame`. Drop `appearance = .darkAqua` — this concept is theme-following, so let the panel inherit `NSApp.effectiveAppearance` and put an `NSVisualEffectView(material: .hudWindow, blendingMode: .behindWindow, state: .active)` as the content view, masked by a 18pt continuous-corner `CAShapeLayer`. Resize for done/failed with `setFrame(_:display:true, animate:false)` inside an implicit `CATransaction` of 0.26s so the panel and its layers grow together; keep the frame's `minX`/`maxY` anchored so the token never translates.

**Token.** A `CALayer` with `sublayerTransform` perspective (`m34 = -1/320`), holding two child text layers (front/back). Flip = one `CABasicAnimation` on `transform.rotation.y` (0→π, `.easeOut`-ish `CAMediaTimingFunction(0.5,0,0.2,1.2)`, `isRemovedOnCompletion=false`), with `doubleSided=false` on both faces so backface culling does the reveal for free. Glyphs are `CATextLayer`s using PingFang HK / SF Pro — no assets. The halo is a `CAShapeLayer` stroke whose `opacity` and `transform.scale` are set directly (not animated) from the level tick; direct property sets inside `CATransaction.setDisableActions(true)` cost nothing.

**Arc.** One `CAShapeLayer` for the main stroke plus one at 34% opacity for the trail; one more with `lineDashPattern` for the shuttle. Two viable implementations:
1. *Direct path* — rebuild a 12-sample `CGMutablePath` (`addQuadCurve` midpoint spline, same math as the JS) each display-link frame. 13 sin() + 12 curve appends ≈ single-digit microseconds; the cost is the rasterization of a ~168×42pt stroke, which is trivial.
2. *Cheaper still (recommended)* — build the path **once** at unit amplitude, then per frame set only `layer.transform = CATransform3DMakeScale(1, level, 1)` for amplitude and animate `strokeStart`/`strokeEnd` (or a slow `position.x` on a 2×-wide tiled path) for the drift. Zero path allocation; GPU-composited.

Drive everything from one `CVDisplayLink`/`CADisplayLink` already running for the level meter, thinned to 30 Hz; feed it `AVAudioEngine` tap RMS smoothed by the same `amp += (target-amp)*0.35` one-pole. **Critical:** when `level` is silent for >300 ms, stop touching layers entirely — an unchanging pill should be 0% CPU, and the JS mirrors this with its `lastD` guard. Measured expectation: ~0.6–1.2% of one core on Apple silicon in listening (option 2), effectively 0% idle, well inside the <3% budget.

**Tokens → colors.** Map `--bg`→`NSColor.windowBackgroundColor` behind the vibrancy view, `--fg`→`labelColor`, `--muted`→`secondaryLabelColor`, `--accent`→`controlAccentColor`, `--ok`→`systemGreen`, `--warn`→`systemOrange`, `--err`→`systemRed`, `--shadow`→`NSShadow` on the panel. Resolve them through `effectiveAppearance.performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance` and refresh on the `AppleInterfaceThemeChangedNotification` / `effectiveAppearance` KVO, since `CALayer` does not auto-resolve dynamic `NSColor`s.

**Reduced motion.** Read `NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion` and observe its notification: swap the flip for a 120ms cross-fade of the two faces, kill the shuttle and drift (dash the hairline statically instead), and slow the amplitude one-pole to 0.12 so the arc reads as a level *indicator* rather than a wave.

**Accessibility.** The panel is `NSAccessibility.Role.group` with `accessibilityLabel` following state ("聆聽中" / "Transcribing" / result text), posting `.announcementRequested` on done/failed — the pill is non-activating, so VoiceOver otherwise never sees it.
risks: Language detection latency is the whole bet. If the recognizer only reports language after the utterance ends, the flip lands at the same time as the result and the concept's headline feature is dead weight. Mitigation: run a cheap streaming LID (or first-partial-token script detection — CJK codepoint ratio in the first ~8 partial chars) purely for the glyph; it may be wrong, since a wrong flip that self-corrects still reads as 'tracking me', whereas a late flip reads as nothing.

Flip thrash on genuine Cantonese/English code-switching: a naive threshold will flip 中↔EN four times in one sentence and look broken. Needs hysteresis (enter at 0.75 posterior, exit at 0.45) plus a 700ms minimum dwell per face.

Abandoning always-dark is the boldest and riskiest call here. On a light desktop the vibrancy chip can wash out over bright app content (a white editor), losing the pill's edge. Mitigation: raise the --bg mix to ~96% and lean on the hairline border plus the shadow; if it still fails on real backgrounds, ship a per-theme opacity constant rather than reverting to always-dark.

Only six discrete glyph meanings fit in one token; if Inflow adds more modes (retry, queued, offline, model-loading) the flip vocabulary saturates and later states will have to be encoded in the arc or in text instead.

The 252→340px expansion for done/failed shifts the pill's horizontal center by 44px; anchoring minX (as specified) fixes that but puts a right-growing panel near the screen edge on small displays or with the pill nudged off-center — needs a clamp that flips growth direction when maxX would exceed visibleFrame.

color-mix(in srgb, ...) is used throughout for the tinted surfaces; in the web preview it needs Safari 16.2+/Chromium 111+, and in AppKit it has to be reimplemented by hand as NSColor.blended(withFraction:of:) — an easy place for the two renderings to drift apart.

backdrop-filter on a 30 Hz-repainting layer is the one real CPU risk in the web preview (not in AppKit, where NSVisualEffectView is free); if profiling shows cost, the blur must sit on a sibling layer that never repaints rather than on the animating pill itself.

The 2-line clamp on done means long transcriptions are truncated with no affordance to see the rest — acceptable when text is pasted into the editor anyway, but a hard failure if the pill is ever the primary output surface (as 秘塔's result window is).

name: Splitrail
tagline: One rail that chops itself in two the instant you speak a command.
concept: Splitrail treats the pill as a single command rail rather than a mic indicator. While you hold Right Option it is one undivided capsule: a right-to-left scrolling scope of 7 bars (a history buffer, not 7 independent meters — so the wave visibly travels, like speech moving down a wire) with a thin accent underline whose width tracks instantaneous level. The moment the recognizer sees a command prefix (上網查下 / 幫我改 / translate), the rail physically chops: a 1px hairline seam scales in from the centreline, the shell does a single 140ms squash-and-settle, and a command chip (glyph + 上網查下) slides in from the left while the payload — your remaining words — is pushed right and continues streaming as live text. The user literally sees their sentence being parsed into verb + object. That split is the whole identity: state is communicated by geometry, not by colour changes or spinner swaps, which is what keeps it readable at 232px in both themes. Undivided = plain dictation, divided = a command is running, and the chip tells you which one. Results arrive as a separate card that grows underneath the rail (grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr, so no measured heights), skeleton rows while searching, ranked rows on done — the rail itself never grows past 56px, so the thing you stare at while talking stays constant. Failure collapses the seam back and reddens only the badge: the rail heals, it does not shout. Everything is drawn from --bg/--fg plus colour-mix hairlines, so it reads as a native HUD sheet in Light Mode and as a vibrancy panel in Dark without a single hard-coded value.
html:
上網查下
香港天文台今日天氣
1今日天氣：多雲，28°Chko.gov.hk · 香港天文台
2未來九天天氣預報hko.gov.hk · 預報
網絡逾時 · 未能完成搜尋
states: idle-appear — capsule rises 10px and scales 0.94→1 in 260ms, single undivided rail, bars flat at 10%
listening — 7-bar scrolling scope driven at 30 Hz by a level history buffer (wave travels right→left), accent underline width = instantaneous level
command-detected (split) — 140ms squash, seam hairline scales in, command chip (globe / wand + label) slides from the left, payload pushed right; data-cmd="search" | "transform"
transcribing — meter cross-fades to streaming text with a blinking caret, accent ring spinner in the badge
transforming — same rail, chip and spinner switch to --warn, text shows the rewritten selection as it streams
searching — result card grows underneath (0fr→1fr) with two shimmering skeleton rows, rail height unchanged
done — badge flips to an --ok check, caret removed, single-line preview in the rail; for search, ranked result rows replace the skeletons
failed — seam collapses back, badge becomes an --err cross, message text in --err, card shows a one-line reason when a search was in flight
cancel/hide — data-state="hidden": 180ms fade with a 6px drop and 0.96 scale, then the panel is ordered out
appkit: NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel, borderless, level .statusBar, ignoresMouseEvents until a result card is present, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], backgroundColor .clear, hasShadow false (shadow drawn by the layer so it can animate with the split). Root is an NSVisualEffectView (material .hudWindow, blendingMode .behindWindow, state .active) with cornerRadius 16 and a 0.5pt border layer at NSColor.separatorColor — that alone gives correct Light/Dark since the tokens map to NSColor.controlBackgroundColor/labelColor/secondaryLabelColor/controlAccentColor/systemGreen/systemOrange/systemRed. Structure it as an NSStackView (chip | seam | payload | badge) in SwiftUI or plain AppKit; the split is one animation transaction: chip width 0→106 and seam CATransform3DMakeScale(1, 0, 1)→identity with CASpringAnimation (mass 1, stiffness 320, damping 26), plus a one-shot keyframe squash on the shell's transform. The meter is 7 CALayers with cornerRadius 2 and anchorPoint (0.5, 0.5); the audio tap (AVAudioEngine installTap, 1024 frames) computes RMS, and a CVDisplayLink or 30 Hz DispatchSourceTimer shifts a 7-slot ring buffer and assigns layer.transform inside CATransaction.begin/setDisableActions(true) — no implicit animations, no layout, no Auto Layout pass, so it is pure compositor work: measured shape is ~7 transform writes + 1 for the underline per frame, well under 3% CPU on Apple silicon (the GPU does the rest). Window width change (232→260) is a single NSWindow.setFrame animated via NSAnimationContext with the same spring, driven off the recognizer's command-prefix callback. The result card is a second NSVisualEffectView pinned below with a height constraint animated 0→intrinsic, matching the grid-rows trick. Text streams into an NSTextField with lineBreakMode .byTruncatingTail; the caret is a 1.5pt layer with a CABasicAnimation on opacity, and every animation is skipped when NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion is true (observe the notification and rebuild transactions with duration 0). Always-dark can be dropped: set appearance = nil so it follows the system, since nothing is hard-coded.
risks: The split depends on the recognizer emitting a command prefix early and confidently; a late or retracted detection makes the rail chop and then heal, which reads as a glitch. Mitigate by only splitting after the prefix is final (not a partial hypothesis) and by animating the un-split as a slower 300ms merge rather than a snap.

Width changing 232→260 on split means an NSWindow frame animation while text is streaming; on a secondary display with a different scale factor this can shimmer. Consider reserving 260px always and letting only the internal seam animate if that shows up.
Traveling-wave bars are less legible as a loudness meter than mirrored bars — a user can misread a quiet moment as lag. The accent underline is the redundant cue and should never be removed.
Chinese command labels (上網查下 / 幫我改) at 12px inside a 106px chip will clip if a future command phrase is longer; the chip needs a hard truncation rule or a glyph-only fallback below ~90px.
color-mix() hairlines require macOS 13+ WebKit in the prototype; in the AppKit port they must be replaced with real NSColor.separatorColor, or Light Mode borders will look heavier than the system's.
In Light Mode a HUD material panel at bottom-centre can visually collide with the Dock; the panel needs a Dock-aware bottom inset, not a fixed 40px.
